pageCache.text:
WELCOME FROM THE HEADTEACHER - Elizabeth Derham
I am delighted to introduce you to Groombridge St Thomas Church of England Primary School. We are a small, friendly primary school situated in the heart of the village of Groombridge on the East Sussex/Kent border. Our purpose and overall aims are to aspire for excellence in every area of the life of our school, to enable children to flourish and fulfill their potential, leaving us as well-rounded and confident individuals. We want all of our pupils to flourish and fulfill their potential academically and in their spiritual, social, moral and cultural development. Understanding and promoting well-being and character development is very important to us at St Thomas'.
Our school values underpin everything that we do in school

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - Wrap Around Care
pageCache.text:
Wrap around care
Breakfast club
Breakfast club is open every day from 7.30am until the start of the school day and costs £6.50 per session. We offer a light breakfast of croissants, toppings, cereals and juice. Spaces for each session can be booked via the Arbor parent portal.
Afterschool club
Afterschool club is open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and is run by an outside provide. Sessions run from 3.15pm-5.15pm and cost £16 per session. To book a session please contact marthakench@aol.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - Lunch
pageCache.text:
Lunch
School Meals
Children can have school meals or bring in a packed lunch to school.
School meals are cooked on-site and provided by Chartwells.
Menus are changed termly and work on a 3 week cycle with something for everyone.
To book a lunch for your child please use ParentPay.
Pupils in Reception, Year 1, and Year 2 are entitled to a funded lunch.
If you are in receipt of certain benefits and think you may be entitled to Free School Meals (including in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2) please speak to the school office.
Packed Lunch
Packed lunches should be sent in a named lunch box. We kindly ask that nuts are not sent in children’s lunchboxes due to allergies; this includes peanut butter/Nutella or any nut bars as this can trigger a serious reaction in some children.

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - School Uniform
pageCache.text:
School Uniform
All children must be sent to school in uniform that adheres to the school uniform policy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
I am delighted to introduce you to Groombridge St Thomas Church of England Primary School. We are a small, friendly primary school situated in the heart of the village of Groombridge, on the border between East Sussex/Kent. In September 2025, we became part of the Pioneer Federation and work in partnership with seven other small village schools.
Our vision is to aspire for excellence in every area to enable children to flourish and fulfil their potential, leaving us as well-rounded and confident individuals.
Our school vision: 'Flourishing in the love of God, we love others as ourselves.'
We want all of our pupils to flourish and fulfil their potential academically and in their spiritual, social, moral, and cultural development. Understanding and promoting well-being and character development is very important to us at St Thomas'.
Alongside our vision, our school values of EXCELLENCE ENTHUSIASM COMPASSION underpin everything that we do in school.
Throughout our school, you will see:
our nurturing, holistic, and caring ethos and values
an engaging, creative, broad and balanced curriculum embedding the arts, music and sport - we are very pleased to have achieved Gold Mark standard for Sport/PE and Healthy School status
the consistently high aspirations and expectations of all our staff and governors
the ongoing support received from parents, the PTA, St Thomas' Church and the wider community
Visits to the school are warmly welcome. Please contact the school office to arrange.

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
As part of the Pioneer Federation, our curriculum at Groombridge St Thomas uses the National Curriculum (2014) as a starting point for teaching a rich curriculum that enables our pupils to know more, do more and remember more. The learning in each subject is carefully sequenced from Reception to Year 6, to ensure that children build on what they already know.
Through our vision of ' Flourishing in the love of God, we love others as ourselves' and our values of EXCELLENCE and ENTHUSIASM, we strive for high expectations from both staff and pupils to enable our pupils to flourish.
In EYFS and KS1 we place a strong emphasis on ensuring pupils develop the key skills for learning alongside ensuring every child can read well. We use Soundswrite to teach phonics and Dandelion readers is our core reading scheme.
Personal and physical development are also key features of our curriculum as we aim to develop the whole child. Our curriculum is enriched through pupil leadership opportunities so that by the time pupils leave Groombridge, they are resilient and resourceful ready to face the next challenge in their life. We are very proud to hold the School Games Gold Mark Award.
Extra-curricular activities
There is a range of extra-curriculum activities on offer including many clubs, piano lessons, visitors and events.

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
Meeting the needs of children with SEN and disabilities.
The school’s vision for SEN provision is that starting with an holistic view of each individual and working in collaboration with pupils, parents/carers and other agencies, we will provide effective class based provision for all pupils with SEND, alongside a structured, targeted intervention programme to ensure we use our best endeavours to enable all pupils to receive timely, early intervention as needed to aid their access to learning.
We are committed to meeting the needs of children with SEND in line with our duties under the Children and Families Act 2014, and the Equalities Act 2010. This is achieved through a whole school approach to the ‘assess, plan, do, review’ cycle to identify needs, plan timely provision and adapt provision based on regular reviews of progress towards agreed outcomes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Groombridge St. Thomas CE Primary School	 - Admissions
pageCache.text:
Admissions
Groombridge St Thomas CE Primary School is pleased to welcome children from Groombridge and the surrounding towns and villages. Our current pupils come from Groombridge village itself and as far afield as Tunbridge Wells, Crowborough and East Grinstead.
Consultation on admission arrangements for Groombridge St Thomas CE Primary School for 2027 to 2028 academic year
Notice is hereby given in accordance with legislation that the governing board, as the admission authority for Groombridge CE Primary School is formally consulting on its proposed admission arrangements and admission criteria for the school year 2027-28.
The 6 week (minimum) consultation will begin on Monday 24 November 2025 with the closing date for submitting comments being midnight on Monday 5 January 2026. All comments are reviewed and considered before the policy is determined by the board.
In determining distance from the school, measurements between home and school will now be measured using the LA’s geographical information system (GIS).
Allocating places and tie breaker
When deciding between applicants who have equal entitlements under the above criteria priority will be given to those children whose home address is nearest to the school using straight line distance. This will be measured using the LA’s geographical information system (GIS). In the event that two or more applications are tied for the last place, the place will be allocated by random allocation, that is, the drawing of lots overseen by a person independent of the school.
Applying for a Reception place
If you are applying for a place for your child to start in our Reception class, please come and visit our wonderful village school. Visits can be booked by contacting the school office. Currently, we can admit up to 15 pupils in our Reception year.
Applications for pupils to start in Reception 2026 close on 15th January 2026. Applications should be made via the Local Authority where you live e.g. East Sussex, Kent.
Admission arrangements for pupils applying for a Reception place, including how we consider applications for a place and how parents can appeal if the application is unsuccessful, can be found in our Admissions Policy below.
Children of parents, either or both, who are regular worshipers at a Christian church, should fill in and return the supplementary application form.
In-year admissions and appeals
We currently have spaces in other year groups should you be looking for a place for your child at Groombridge St Thomas. Visits to the school are warmly welcome. Please contact the school office to arrange a visit.
Applications should be made via East Sussex County Council.
If your application to us is unsuccessful and you wish to make an appeal, details of the appeal process and the dates by which you must appeal by can be found on the ESCC admissions page by clicking on the link below.
